dossier.public_summary: The signal is deep, flat-bottomed and repeated, but its depth jumps between data pipelines and between individual transits and a secondary eclipse is present at about one-third of the orbit. Gaia already flags the star as a binary with high astrometric excess. Together this is the signature of a blended stellar eclipse, not a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by >100% between sectors (3256, 1185, 1595 ppm, chi2 44.14 dof 2) but sector_depths_by_source verdict differs_by_source: QLP 3256 ppm vs SPOC 2-min 1303 ppm steady within SPOC, so change is pipeline-dependent, not single-source instability
Individual transits inconsistent: mean 1633 ppm, outlier epoch -16 depth 4024 ppm sigma 7.5, chi2 67.86267446905642 dof 3, share_of_top_3 0.929 indicates dip dominated by few/depth-changing events
Secondary dip detected at phase 0.2824 depth 456.1 ppm depth_over_dip 0.2778 with snr 6.618 well above best_brightening_snr 3.428, favouring stellar companion over planet which should have none

Gaia astrometry indicates resolved binarity; target is an EB/blended binary, not an isolated planet host. Planet size 3.554 Rearth and flat bottom (v_sigma -3.514) are compatible with small star eclipse diluted to planet size
